posts.text: Single-Agent AI Coding Is a Nightmare for Engineers — X Article (tweet body is t.co image link; real payload is an Article titled 'Single-agent AI coding is a nightmare for engineers'). Introduces the Kitchen Brigade metaphor (Head Chef/Line Cook = Orchestrator/Subagent) and a 5-pattern framework for multi-agent coding. Pattern 5 = separate builder from verifier ('Here comes Gordon Ramsay').
posts.notes: ALREADY INGESTED as full post entry (2026-04-17). 2.76:1 bookmark-to-like is top 1% of practitioner save ratios we've seen. Pattern 5 = our review-fix loop Step 5 = external validation from Cerebras Head of DevX. Kitchen Brigade metaphor is a cleaner frame than Orchestrator/Subagent for non-technical audiences — steal for client pitches. 'Stop being a one-shot Sloperator' is 2026's '10x engineer' coinage. Cerebras marketing bias visible (Codex Spark in every pattern story) but framework is portable.

article.title: The Year of Latency Debt (And How Big Tech Is Paying It Down)
article.preview_text: (reposted from my blog sarahchieng.com/blog) Over the past several years, we've spent enormous resources making AI models more capable, bigger, smarter, and more contextually aware. What we haven't [made them is fast enough to keep a human in the loop]

posts.notes: Cross-posted X-article of her Cerebras blog essay. Core thesis: 2026 is the year latency debt comes due; multi-agent/coding/voice/HITL workloads are sequential+memory-bound+latency-sensitive; GPUs are the wrong architecture for that shape. 0.92 bookmark-to-like ratio (34/37) is a tell — this is a save-for-later piece, not a viral take. Direct validation of our harness bet: the binding constraint in 2026 is token SPEED, not token quantity. Pair with Vincent Kottsch's AIE Europe line 'not wasting tokens'. CANDIDATE for full /ingest-post — this is the cleanest single-phrase articulation of the 2026 thesis I've seen.

posts.text: I graduated from MIT in 2023. It was the year (more like era) when it was especially hard to get a role in big tech. A lot of my friends and classmates basically took two alternative routes > get a masters/higher education and wait it out > build or join a startup. it's been a few years now, and those life choices are starting to realize. For me personally, I reneged a quant trading job and moved to SF instead (for my own reasons). But it's been really beautiful to see the companies/achievements everyone has built and accomplished in the past few years in sf, nyc, etc.
posts.notes: Personal career reflection. 111K views + 744 likes = high-engagement identity post. Context for who she is (MIT 2023 cohort, reneged quant offer for SF), but no technical or harness content. Useful only for practitioner profile background.

posts.text: Stop Shipping AI Slop: How Codex Spark Changes The Way You Code — 9 practices for GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark at 1,200+ tok/s on Cerebras WSE. Pinned on her X profile.
posts.notes: Authored blog post (not a tweet). 9 practices for fast-inference pair programming: (1) pair-programmer not delegatee, (2) cheap validation, (3) explore multiple paths, (4) single sessions (2-3 max), (5) 128K as working memory + fresh sessions, (6) AGENTS.md + PLAN.md external memory, (7) hybrid models (Codex for planning, Spark for execution), (8) strict guardrails, (9) continuous doc-gardening via CI. 80% overlap with our tmux-orchestrator playbook — this is external validation of our patterns. CANDIDATE for full /ingest-article.

posts.text: The Debate of MCP vs. CLI Centers on Speed — Sarah Chieng is acknowledged as reviewer. Central thesis: MCP 55K tokens of tool defs vs CLI opacity; real fix is faster inference (Cerebras 3000 tok/s) + secure execution (Monty 0.06ms vs Docker 195ms).
posts.notes: Reviewer credit, not author. But the thesis is directly relevant: MCP overhead is a real problem (55K tokens for GitHub+Slack+Sentry), CLIs are faster but opaque, answer is not protocol choice but faster inference + secure sandboxing. Ties to our pi-mcp-adapter catalogue entry (50-100x token reduction). Monty at 0.06ms startup is new to us — candidate for tool catalogue. CANDIDATE for /ingest-article.
